Stack'd — the user journey

Stack'd is a privacy-first personal finance tracker for iPhone and Android: every account, transaction and budget lives on the phone, nothing is sent anywhere. This page walks three people through the app as it ships today (version 1.2, English, light theme), screen by screen, with the friction we see and the questions we would like a designer's view on.

Build 1.2 (build 10202 round), 8 November 2026Platform iPhone and Android, portrait; screenshots 390 × 844Data invented example finances, the same seed on every screenChecks each step has an automated journey test where one was possible (see Coverage)
The app in one minuteThree peopleNora · first timeMarco · dailyLea · power userEvery screenCoverageFindings and questions

The app in one minute

You create accounts (the app also calls them wallets: a bank account, a card, cash, savings) with an opening balance, then log what you earn, spend and move between them. Balances are never typed in: they are always the sum of the entries. Everything else — the Home graph, Goals (monthly limits per category), Analytics, Smart Insights — is computed from those entries, on the phone.

Money entered by hand is the heart of it, but data can also come in from a bank statement file, a MoneyStats or QIF export, or a Stack'd backup, and go out as a CSV, a PDF of receipts or a one-file backup. There is no login and no server: the free plan allows two accounts and the built-in categories; a one-time Stack'd Pro purchase lifts both limits. An optional bank-connection feature exists in the code but is not in the shipped build, so it is not covered here.

The interface is one scrolling screen at a time, a five-tab bar at the bottom and a round + button that opens the quick-actions menu. Sheets slide up from the bottom for pickers and confirmations. Light and dark themes, five languages (English, French, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese).

Home

Total balance with two deltas (today and projected end of month), a two-pane graph (balance curve · monthly net), the wallet cards in your order, and the widgets you chose.

History

Every entry by day, one month at a time (‹ › or a Period sheet), filters as chips, swipe a row for Paid / Edit / Delete, long press to select many.

Goals

Monthly limits per category with a ring (Allocated · Spent · Remaining), bars that turn amber then red, rollover month to month.

Analytics

Net balance for the period with the change vs the previous one, income − expenses per bucket, and the category distribution ring.

Smart Insights

A page of plain-language cards: budgets at risk, unusual spending, pace vs last month, upcoming payments, loan progress… each opens where you can act.

Loans

A simulator for a mortgage, personal loan or installment plan (full schedule, early repayments, rate changes), kept as a simulation or tracked as a real loan tied to a recurring payment.

How the screens connect

Full-screen pages (New Log, New Account, the editors, Loans, Import, Export, Backup, In-app purchases) carry a round ✕ at the top right and return to where you came from. Sheets close with ✕, Cancel, a tap outside or the phone's Back.

Three people

The journeys below follow three invented users whose habits cover the app end to end. They are not research personas; they are a way to walk every screen in the order a real person would meet it.

N

Nora · first-time user

Installed the app this morning after giving up on a spreadsheet. Two accounts, logs by hand, privacy-minded: she picked Stack'd because it asks for no bank login.

Goal. See where her money is by tonight, with as little setup as possible.

Worry. Getting the first numbers wrong and not knowing how to fix them.

Success. Her two balances on Home, a first expense in History, one budget set — and a clear idea of what Pro would add.

M

Marco · daily logger

Six months in: four accounts, a few budgets, a card he uses for almost everything. Opens the app most evenings to log the day and glance at the month.

Goal. Log three things in under a minute each and know whether the month is on track.

Worry. Duplicates, a recurring payment he forgot about, a budget blown without noticing.

Success. Entries logged with tags and a transfer, the streaming subscription set to repeat, Goals and Insights read in passing.

L

Lea · power user

Brings in her bank statement every month, keeps backups, tracks a mortgage, and tunes the app to her taste — order of accounts and tabs, hidden balances in public, Italian at home.

Goal. Move the month's bank data in without duplicates and keep everything backed up.

Worry. An import that doubles her entries; losing data on a new phone.

Success. Statement imported and categorised with rules, a backup saved, the mortgage tracked, the app arranged her way.

Nora · the first hour

From the first launch to the moment the free plan asks for Pro. Nora starts with an empty install, picks EUR and English, creates two accounts and logs her first expense.

1

Arrive

the Welcome sheet and an empty Home
N1 · Welcome to Stack'd

Pick a currency and a language

Does
Opens the app for the first time. Sets Currency to EUR and Language to English, taps Get Started.
Sees
A mandatory sheet over a blank Home: "Set your preferred region. You can always change this later in Others → Region Setting." Two rows (Currency, Language) and one button. It cannot be swiped away.
Friction
FrictionNothing says what the app does or what happens next; the only choices are two settings. A returning user who wants to bring data from another app has no door here (import is five taps deep in Others).
Ask
QuestionShould the first screen say what Stack'd is and offer two starts — "Start fresh" and "Bring my data" — before the region question?

Automated · journey_first_time

N2 · Home (empty)

An empty dashboard

Does
Looks around.
Sees
Total Balance €0.00 with two zero deltas, an empty graph area with the range chips, the Add Wallet tile alone in the wallets row, a Latest transactions widget saying "No transactions yet".
Friction
FrictionThree empty states compete (hero, graph, widget). The one action that matters — create an account — is a small dashed tile; the + button is not pointed at.
Ask
QuestionWould a single first-run card ("Add your first account to see your balance here") replace the empty graph and widget until there is data?

Automated · journey_first_time

The + menu

Does
Taps +.
Sees
Five actions over a dimmed Home: Add Log, Add Account, Debt, Add Category, Others & Settings.
Friction
FrictionThe entry says Debt; the page it opens is titled Loans. "Add Category" sits at the same level as "Add Log" though it is rare. Settings are reachable only from here (there is no gear anywhere else).
Ask
QuestionRename the entry to Loans; demote Add Category; is Settings behind + what you would expect, or does it want a place in the top bar of Home?

N4 · New Account

Create "Main Bank"

Does
Taps Add Account. Types "Main Bank", leaves type Bank, keeps the first colour, types the opening balance 1,200.00 and taps Create Account.
Sees
Account Name, Type, Icon, Account Color (a row of dots), Currency (EUR), Opening Balance with Positive / Negative, Opening Balance Date (today), Set as Default Wallet. Save at the bottom.
Friction
FrictionThe opening-balance field is digits-only and shifts right to left (typing 1-2-0-0-0-0 shows 1,200.00): fast once known, surprising the first time. Eight account types and eight colours arrive before the user knows what they are for.
Ask
QuestionIs the cents-shift amount entry the right pattern here (it matches the transaction form), or should this field accept a typed "1200"?

Read the first day

What this journey tells us. Nora reaches her goal: two balances, one expense, one limit. The rough edges are at the very start (an onboarding that explains nothing and three empty states), in the first History read (the opening balance posing as a transaction), and in the length of the New Log form for a one-line action.

A monthly streaming subscription

Automated · journey_daily

What this journey tells us. Marco's evening works: each log is a minute, and the month is readable in Goals and Analytics. The friction is in discoverability (swipes, the pager, the card-tap filter) and in density (the Home header, the Insights cards, the scope sheet).

What this journey tells us. Everything Lea needs exists and works, but all of it is two or three taps into Others & Settings, and the Data screens (Import, Map Columns, Review) ask for more reading than the rest of the app.

Findings and questions

What the journey tests and the walk-through turned up. Bugs were fixed as they were found; the rest are design questions for the review.

#KindWhatOutcome
1FixedThe third tab is named Goals everywhere (bar, manual, insights) but its page was titled Budget (Presupuesto / Orçamento in Spanish and Portuguese).The page is now titled like its tab in all five languages.
2Design questionAn account's opening balance is a transaction row in History ("Adjustment +€1,200.00", dated the day the account was created). On the first day it dominates the day sum and the Net Change (N7).Kept as designed; see question 2 below.
3Design questionFuture occurrences of a recurring payment are real rows dated ahead; they are not counted in today's balance, but they look like any other row when you step to a later month (M7).Kept as designed; see question 4 below.
4ObservationTwo names for one place: the + menu says Debt, the page says Loans; the menu says Others & Settings, the page says Others.Not changed; question 1 below.
5ObservationIn the test browser, a flung sideways swipe on the Home graph pager can leave it between panes and swallow the next tap; a swipe that pauses before lifting snaps correctly. Not reproduced by hand on a phone.Noted for the engineering backlog; no change.
6ObservationClosing a sheet starts a 300 ms clean-up; a second sheet opened inside that window (possible only in automation) can be swept away.Noted for the engineering backlog; no change.

Questions for the designer

  1. Naming. Debt vs Loans, Others vs Others & Settings, Dashboard vs Home: one name per place?
  2. Opening balance. Should it be a row in History at all; if so, named and styled as what it is and left out of the day sum and Net Change?
  3. First run. Should Welcome say what the app is and offer "Start fresh" / "Bring my data"; and should an empty Home show one call to action instead of three empty states?
  4. Future rows. How should upcoming recurring payments look in History, and should Paid default to off for a date in the future?
  5. New Log. Amount and category first, the rest behind "More"? A visual category picker instead of a dropdown?
  6. Home hierarchy. Which one question should Home answer first — total, this month's net, or on-track — and do both deltas earn their place?
  7. Discoverability. Row swipes, the graph pager, the card tap, hold-to-drag: which deserve a hint, and how?
  8. Density. Insights cards, the recurring scope sheet, the currency switch sheet, Goals rows (ring + percentage + bar): where to cut?
  9. Data screens. Should Import / Export / Backup be a top-level destination rather than cards in Others; can Map Columns show sample values and Review group identical descriptions?
  10. Free plan. Show "2 of 2 accounts" before the wall; hide the empty Subscriptions tab?
